The UN Security Council convened an emergency session to debate a ceasefire resolution for the Gaza Strip after months of intense fighting.
France formally tabled a ceasefire resolution at the UN Security Council, demanding an immediate halt to hostilities.
Washington announced a fresh package of sanctions targeting Russian state banks and defence contractors in response to continued military operations in Ukraine.
Multiple NATO countries pledged artillery, ammunition and air-defence systems to Ukraine as part of a coordinated support package agreed at the alliance summit.
India was elected by the UN General Assembly to serve a two-year term as a non-permanent member of the Security Council.
Brazilian President Lula da Silva delivered the opening address at the UN General Assembly in New York, calling for reform of global governance institutions.
EU member states and the European Parliament reached a historic deal on the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, establishing common rules for processing asylum seekers.
The People's Liberation Army launched large-scale naval and air exercises encircling Taiwan, described by Beijing as a warning against separatist forces.
The ICC issued an arrest warrant for a sitting head of government, marking one of the few times the court has targeted an incumbent leader.
Pakistan conducted parliamentary elections under heavy security, with opposition parties alleging widespread irregularities and supporters of the PTI party protesting across major cities.
The US House of Representatives approved a 95 billion dollar supplemental aid package for Ukraine, Israel and Taiwan, which was subsequently signed into law.
Iran launched more than 300 ballistic missiles and drones at Israel in an unprecedented direct attack, most of which were intercepted by Israeli and allied air defences.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed a joint session of the US Congress in Washington, receiving a standing ovation from many legislators.
Donald Trump was found guilty on all 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in a New York state court, becoming the first former US president convicted of a crime.
President Joe Biden announced he was ending his re-election campaign and endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris as the Democratic nominee.
The Federal Reserve lifted its benchmark interest rate to a range not seen in over two decades as it continued its campaign against persistent inflation.
The Food and Agriculture Organization reported that its food price index declined for the third month in a row, driven by lower cereal and vegetable oil prices.
Germany recorded two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth, officially meeting the definition of a technical recession for the first time since the pandemic.
Bitcoin reached a new all-time high of over 70 000 dollars, driven by institutional inflows following the approval of spot Bitcoin ETFs in the United States.
The International Monetary Fund trimmed its 2024 global growth projection citing high borrowing costs, slowing trade and persistent geopolitical tensions.
India surpassed Japan in nominal GDP terms according to World Bank data, making it the fourth-largest economy globally after the United States, China and Germany.
The OPEC+ alliance announced it would maintain voluntary crude oil production cuts into the fourth quarter of 2024 to support prices.
Apple Inc crossed the three trillion dollar market capitalisation milestone, becoming the first publicly traded company in history to achieve this valuation.
The World Bank announced a 25 billion dollar climate finance package aimed at helping low- and middle-income countries transition to cleaner energy and adapt to rising temperatures.
UK inflation dropped to its lowest level since 2021, with the Consumer Prices Index falling sharply as energy costs eased and food price growth slowed.
The US national debt crossed 34 trillion dollars in January 2024, raising fresh concerns about the country's fiscal trajectory.
The Japanese yen weakened past 160 yen per dollar, reaching its lowest point since 1990 as the Bank of Japan maintained ultra-loose monetary policy.
Reports emerged that NEOM, Saudi Arabia's flagship futuristic city project, faced cost estimates that had soared to over one trillion dollars, far above initial projections.
Global temperature data from multiple agencies confirmed that 2023 surpassed all previous records to become the hottest year in recorded history.
Water levels in the Amazon River reached historic lows in 2023, with scientists declaring the drought the most severe since at least 1979.
For the first time in UN climate talks history, COP28 produced a text calling for a transition away from fossil fuels.
Arctic sea ice reached its lowest recorded September extent since satellite measurements began, alarming climate scientists tracking polar warming.
Canadian wildfires burned over 18 million hectares in 2023, destroying communities and blanketing North American cities in smoke.
A report from the Global Carbon Project estimated that CO2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion reached a record high of approximately 36.8 billion tonnes in 2023.
Unprecedented monsoon rains caused flooding across one-third of Pakistan in 2022, displacing 33 million people.
The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report concluded that without immediate emissions reductions, global warming would likely exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius in the 2030s.
The Australian parliament passed a motion declaring a national climate emergency, committing the government to stronger emissions reduction targets.
Solar power generated more electricity than coal across European Union member states for the first time in recorded history during a summer period.
The World Health Organization declared the mpox outbreak a public health emergency of international concern for the second time, citing a new and more deadly variant spreading in Africa.
WHO recommended the R21 malaria vaccine for use in children, the second malaria vaccine to receive WHO endorsement, following successful trials in Africa.
Researchers from BioNTech and Merck reported promising Phase 2 results from a personalised mRNA vaccine targeting melanoma, showing a 44 percent reduction in recurrence.
The WHO and CDC reported an 18 percent increase in measles cases worldwide in 2023, attributing the surge to pandemic-era disruptions in childhood vaccination.
Semaglutide, marketed as Wegovy, received regulatory approval in the United States, UK and the EU as a treatment for obesity, showing average weight loss of 15 percent in trials.
The US Surgeon General issued an advisory calling for alcohol beverage labels to include explicit cancer risk warnings, citing evidence linking alcohol to at least seven types of cancer.
US health authorities recommended an updated COVID-19 booster dose for adults aged 65 and older and immunocompromised individuals ahead of the winter season.
The WHO published a report naming antimicrobial resistance one of the top global public health threats, warning that drug-resistant infections could kill 10 million people annually by 2050.
US health authorities confirmed a human case of H5N1 avian influenza in a dairy farm worker in Texas in 2024, prompting heightened surveillance of cattle and poultry farms.
OpenAI unveiled GPT-4o, a flagship model capable of accepting and generating text, images and audio in real time, marking a significant advance in multimodal AI.
The EU AI Act, the world's first comprehensive legal framework for artificial intelligence, was adopted by the European Parliament.
Google announced that its Gemini Ultra model outperformed GPT-4 on 30 of 32 academic benchmarks, including the MMLU multitask language understanding test.
Internal documents revealed that X's advertising revenue fell by more than 50 percent in the year following Elon Musk's 44 billion dollar acquisition.
Meta AI released the Llama family of large language models as open-source, allowing researchers and developers to download and modify the models freely.
SpaceX's Starship, the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, completed a full test flight with both the ship and booster recovered successfully.
Apple released the Vision Pro mixed-reality headset at a starting price of 3 499 dollars, marking the company's entry into spatial computing.
The Biden administration expanded export controls on advanced semiconductor chips and AI hardware, blocking sales of the most powerful GPUs to Chinese companies.
Microsoft committed a total of 13 billion dollars in investment to OpenAI, making it the exclusive cloud provider for OpenAI services and gaining a significant equity stake.
The US Congress passed legislation requiring ByteDance to divest TikTok within 270 days or face a ban, citing national security concerns about Chinese ownership.
Fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces displaced more than eight million people within Sudan, creating the world's largest internal displacement crisis.
Houthi forces in Yemen launched drone and missile attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea, forcing major shipping companies to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope.
Sweden formally joined NATO as its 32nd member after Hungary ratified its accession protocol, completing a process that began following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
The Israeli Defense Forces began a ground operation in Rafah in southern Gaza in May 2024, drawing widespread international condemnation.
Russian forces launched large-scale missile and drone strikes targeting Ukraine's electricity generation and transmission network during winter 2024.

Myanmar's military government lost control of significant territory in border regions as coordinated offensives by ethnic armed organisations and the People's Defence Force overwhelmed junta positions.
The UN declared a severe humanitarian crisis in Somalia after consecutive failed rainy seasons left over 6 million people facing acute food insecurity.
Armed gangs took control of large parts of Port-au-Prince and other Haitian cities in 2024, effectively paralysing government functions and prompting a call for international intervention.
Spain defeated England 2-1 in the UEFA Euro 2024 final in Berlin, claiming their fourth European Championship title.
Carlos Alcaraz defeated Novak Djokovic in the Wimbledon final to retain his title and claim his second Wimbledon crown.
The Paris 2024 Summer Olympic Games took place from 26 July to 11 August, featuring opening ceremonies on the River Seine.
India advanced to the ICC T20 World Cup 2024 final held in Barbados, defeating England in the semi-final.
Real Madrid defeated Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League final at Wembley Stadium, claiming a record-extending 15th European Cup title.
Swedish athlete Armand Mondo Duplantis cleared 6.25 metres at the Paris Olympics to set a new pole vault world record.
Basketball star Caitlin Clark was selected first overall by the Indiana Fever in the 2024 WNBA Draft, generating record interest in the league.
Max Verstappen clinched his fourth consecutive Formula One Drivers' Championship in 2024, cementing his place among the sport's all-time greats.
Health authorities worldwide confirmed that there is no scientific evidence linking 5G telecommunications infrastructure to COVID-19 or any other viral infection.
All 50 US states and the District of Columbia certified their 2020 presidential election results, and Congress confirmed Joe Biden's victory on 7 January 2021.
Regulatory agencies, manufacturers and independent scientists confirmed that approved COVID-19 vaccines contain no tracking devices, microchips or nanobots.
The World Health Organization recommended against the use of ivermectin for COVID-19 treatment outside clinical trials, citing insufficient evidence of benefit.
Multiple systematic reviews found no credible scientific evidence that wind turbine noise or electromagnetic fields cause cancer in nearby residents.
Aviation experts and atmospheric scientists explain that aircraft contrails are water vapour that freezes around particles from engine exhaust, not chemical agents intentionally sprayed.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky continued to appear publicly in Kyiv and internationally through 2024, refuting repeated claims of his death or flight from Ukraine.
George Soros is a private citizen who made his fortune in currency speculation and philanthropy; he has never held any elected or appointed government office.
Independent audits of WHO mortality data found no evidence of systematic manipulation; death counts were based on standard excess mortality methodology agreed by member states.
